Reproduce {{asm}} as source that builds to byte-exact matching asm; never hand-edit the asm. First decide the form (`make info`'s `(default)` tool line is fallback flags, not proof of C). Write {{c}} (K&R C for the Manx Aztec `cc`) only if `cc` could have generated this code; otherwise write {{s}} (Manx `as` assembly{{style}}). Signs it is hand-written: a call `cc` would not emit (arg already in a register, no push/pop); a counter in a register `register` cannot get; no `csav` where C has locals, or the body runs in its caller's frame; segment-register juggling (`push cs; pop ds`); `cld` and string ops; code-segment data; padding `nop`s or jumps `cc` would shorten; falling through into the next routine. Never put a whole routine body in `#asm` inside a C function: that is what a .s is for, and labels in `#asm` become linker symbols. `#asm` is only for a few instructions inside real C. A .s does `include lmacros.h` — the project's, built from `disassembler/lib/aztec/lmacros_master.h`, which lists each macro's exact expansion. Use its structured blocks `.if`/`.elseif`/`.else`/`.endif`, `.while`/`.endw`, `.repeat`/`.until`, `.break`/`.continue` in place of labels and jumps (conditions `ax == 5`, `al lt 3`, `dl and 2`, `carry?`, `not cx`; no `!`, `<`, `>`), then the call, push/pop, clamp, `procdef`/`pret`, `movseg`, `outp`, `fatal` and `jnear` shorthands; write a custom prologue/epilogue out and plain instructions where no macro fits. Indent each block body one tab past its directive.{{hand}}

Commands (repo root): `make rebuild` is the pass/fail gate: it recompiles every .c/.s, checks it against the original bytes, and assembles. `make refs {{project}} {{binary}} ROUTINE` lists the address-named and content-tagged symbols a routine references (already-named callees are omitted; declare them `extrn` yourself in a .s). `make name {{project}} {{binary}} SYMBOL=NAME[:NOTE] ...` writes the sidecar, renames the hand-written sources and every reference in them (file, routine, `NAME_` in .s, `extern`/`extrn`, C callers), then builds and rebuilds; give SYMBOL as the build spells it (`cseg_0d3a`, `bss_1234`, `io_loc_KRUO`, `{{label}}`) or by its current name, and single-quote any spec whose note has spaces. `make build {{project}}` regenerates the asm from the disassembly and sources. The sidecar ({{sidecar}}) and the tooling under disassembler/ are there to read when you need them.

Steps:
1. Write the source with the routine still named `{{label}}` and run `make rebuild` until it passes. If the only differences left are symbol or label names on the same instructions and offsets, the bytes match: go on to step 2 (step 3's `make name` regenerates the asm). A report that the source compiles to a different size than its fragment means the bytes do not match yet.
2. Give parameters and locals descriptive names in the source itself (C names; `equ` names for .s and #asm stack arguments and locals). Add terse comments that say why, not what: a one-line header above the routine (a `;` line in a .s, `/* */` in C, never `//`), and short trailing comments on loops, branches and magic numbers (BIOS/DOS function numbers, key codes, header offsets, strides, flag bits). Describe only what the code shows; don't guess intent.
3. Run `make refs {{project}} {{binary}} {{label}}`, then name everything in one call: `make name {{project}} {{binary}} {{label}}=NAME:'note' SYMBOL=NAME:'note' ...`. NAME for the routine is a descriptive lowercase_underscore name keeping any prefix its flags need; add every symbol `make refs` listed (globals, code-segment data, called routines, including those only in `extrn` lines) except "label inside" rows, each with a note saying what it holds or does.
4. If `make name` reports a rebuild failure, fix the source and run `make rebuild` until it passes. No address-named or content-tagged symbol may remain in the source.

Your final message: only the routine's new name, or, if you could not finish, what is left and why.

{{guide}}
